metadata.name: leash_program
metadata.description: Leash: capability accounts, issue/attenuate/revoke/redeem. See docs/BUILD_PLAN.md.

docs: Capability program: issue / attenuate / revoke / redeem, plus `record_spend` — the
CPI entrypoint leash-hook calls to commit a spend it has already validated. The
actual cap/expiry/allowlist/revoked checks happen in leash-hook, inside the
Token-2022 transfer itself (docs/BUILD_PLAN.md §4); this program owns the Capability
accounts and is the only one allowed to write `spent`.

accounts.name: child_owner
docs: the parent's owner is the one authorizing this attenuation, not the child.

accounts.name: child_token_account
docs: via CPI, owned by `child_owner` directly (same bearer-object model as `issue`).

accounts.name: vault
docs: time. Its authority is `program_authority` below.

accounts.name: wrapped_mint
docs: configured at deployment time). Mutable because minting increases supply.

accounts.name: capability_token_account
docs: created here via CPI to the associated-token-account program. Owned by
`principal` directly — the capability is a bearer object the holder controls,
not something leash-program gates access to (BUILD_PLAN.md §0).

accounts.name: hook_authority
docs: constraint can't reference a non-`Pubkey::find_program_address`-under-this-program
scheme directly, so the check is manual in the handler). `signer` is required
here, not just checked manually: without it, Anchor's account-type (a plain
`UncheckedAccount`, not `Signer`) makes the *generated CPI instruction itself*
mark `is_signer: false` in its account metas, so `invoke_signed`'s PDA signature
never gets a chance to matter — confirmed by hitting `is_signer == false` here
with a correctly-matching PDA address, not by guessing.

accounts.name: program_authority
docs: one shared authority for the deployment (see constants::AUTHORITY_SEED).

errors.name: CapExceeded
errors.msg: spend would exceed this capability's remaining budget

errors.name: NotAllowlisted
errors.msg: destination is not on this capability's allowlist

errors.name: Revoked
errors.msg: capability, or an ancestor of it, has been revoked

errors.name: NotASubset
errors.msg: child cap/expiry/allowlist is not a subset of the parent's

errors.name: Unauthorized
errors.msg: signer does not own this capability

errors.name: UnauthorizedCaller
errors.msg: only leash-hook may record a spend

types.name: Capability
docs: One node in a capability tree. A root capability has `parent = Pubkey::default()`; an
attenuated child has `parent = <parent Capability pubkey>`.
Invariant (checked by the program, not by convention — see BUILD_PLAN.md §2/§3):
spent + committed_to_children <= cap

fields.name: owner
docs: Signer who may attenuate or revoke this specific node.

fields.name: parent
docs: `Pubkey::default()` (all-zero) for root capabilities, never a real Capability
address otherwise. Deliberately NOT `Option<Pubkey>`: Borsh encodes `Option<T>`
as a 1-byte tag plus 32 bytes only when `Some`, so its on-disk size — and every
field after it — would shift depending on whether a capability has a parent.
leash-hook's extra-account-meta resolution needs `parent` at a **fixed** byte
offset to read it directly out of raw account data (see `PARENT_FIELD_OFFSET`),
so it has to be a fixed-size `Pubkey`, not an `Option`. Found by working through
the hook's account-resolution design, not by guessing — see BUILD_PLAN.md §5.

fields.name: ancestors
docs: `[immediate parent, grandparent, great-grandparent]` (up to `ANCESTOR_SLOTS` =
`MAX_DEPTH`), each `Pubkey::default()` past this capability's actual depth.
Deliberately a **direct copy on this account**, not something leash-hook chains
together by reading each ancestor's own `parent` field one hop at a time — that
approach was tried first (Week 4) and broke: a root capability's `parent` is the
System Program placeholder address, which has zero account data, so trying to
read a "further parent" *out of* that placeholder's data fails at the
client-side resolution step before a transaction is even submitted. Storing the
whole chain here means every ancestor is read from *this* capability's own data
(always real, always populated), never from a potentially-empty placeholder.
Populated by `attenuate`: `[parent, parent.ancestors[0], parent.ancestors[1]]`.

fields.name: token_account
docs: The Token-2022 token account holding this capability's spendable balance.

fields.name: cap
docs: Total this capability may ever spend (cumulative, not a rolling window).

fields.name: spent
docs: Cumulative amount spent so far via the transfer hook's spend path.

fields.name: committed_to_children
docs: Sum of `cap` handed to attenuated children. Not spendable by this node directly.

fields.name: expiry
docs: Unix timestamp. No spend may execute after this.

fields.name: allowlist
docs: Flat allowlist of destinations this capability (and, for now, its children) may
pay. MVP: equality-or-subset check only, no arbitrary narrowing logic yet.

fields.name: revoked
docs: Set by `revoke`. The hook must also check every ancestor's flag, up to MAX_DEPTH.

fields.name: depth
docs: 0 for a root capability; capped at MAX_DEPTH.

constants.name: AUTHORITY_SEED
docs: Single shared PDA used as both the wrapped mint's mint authority (issue mints,
redeem burns don't need it, but a future re-mint might) and the vault's token-account
authority (redeem withdraws real USDC from the vault, signed by this PDA). One PDA
instead of two — nothing here needs them to be separate for the MVP.
